content: 1. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended for use in certain scenarios to avoid potential drug interactions or reduced efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 2. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of cabozantinib by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 3. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of cadexomer iodine through a mechanism involving decreased renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is also unknown. Hyperkalemia should be monitored closely. 4. Ethinylestradiol can increase the levels or effects of caffeine by affecting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic enzyme CYP1A2. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 5. The combination of calaspargase pegol and drospirenone is not recommended due to the potential for an indirect interaction that may reduce the efficacy of oral contraceptives. Alternative or non-oral contraceptive methods should be used for females of childbearing potential. 6. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of calcifediol and calcitriol by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 7. Drospirenone may decrease the levels of calcium acetate, calcium carbonate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, and calcium gluconate by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 8. Drospirenone and canagliflozin both increase serum potassium levels. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 9. Drospirenone and candesartan both increase serum potassium levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 10. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of capmatinib by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 11. Drospirenone and captopril may synergistically increase the risk of hyperkalemia. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 12. Carbamazepine may decrease the levels or effects of drospirenone and ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Alternative contraceptive methods should be used during coadministration and for 28 days after discontinuing therapy to ensure contraceptive reliability. 13. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of carbamazepine by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered due to the potential reduction in hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 14. Drospirenone increases and carbenoxolone decreases serum potassium levels. The effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are advised. 15. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of cariprazine by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 16. Drospirenone and carvedilol both increase serum potassium levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 17. Certain antibiotics, such as cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefepime, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefprozil, ceftazidime, ceftibuten, and cefuroxime, may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Drospirenone and celecoxib both increase serum potassium levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 19. Drospirenone and celiprolol both increase serum potassium levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 20. Cenobamate may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Women should use additional or alternative non-hormonal birth control methods when using cenobamate with oral contraceptives. 21. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of various drugs, including chlorodiazepoxide, chloroquine, chlorpheniramine, ciclosonide, cilostazol, and others, by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 22. Drospirenone increases and certain diuretics, such as chlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, and cyclopenthiazide, decrease serum potassium levels. The effect of these interactions is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are advised. 23. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of cyclophosphamide by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Cyclophosphamide may also increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 24. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels of cyclosporine by an unknown mechanism. Drospirenone and cyclosporine may interact through pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Dabrafenib may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of dabrafenib. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 26. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of daclatasvir by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 27. Danazol may increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 28. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of dantrolene by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 29. Conivaptan may increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered due to the potential for serious interactions. 30. Additional non-hormonal forms of contraception are recommended when using drugs that may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives.
